name: issue-groom
description: A maintainer opens an issue; om-auto-manage-issues adds SDLC labels, a Definition of Ready check and implementation notes (ADR 0017). `authors` is the gate: the run holds Bash with no allowlist, so an issue from anyone else is groomed only when a maintainer adds `groom`. Issues a run holds or a human put on hold never match.

name: issue-regroom
description: A label only a collaborator can set: `groom` re-runs om-auto-manage-issues on one issue (an external report a maintainer vouches for, an edit, a reply). The override removes the label first.

name: issue-autofix
description: A human adds `autofix`; om-auto-fix-issue drives the issue to a reviewed PR on develop (ADR 0017). Held, blocked, do-not-merge or spec-pending issues never match.

name: issue-spec
description: A human adds `spec` to a `feature` issue; om-auto-write-spec lands .ai/specs/<date>-<slug>.md on a design-only PR (ADR 0017).

name: pr-autopilot
description: A human maintainer opens a PR; om-pr-autopilot diagnoses and runs the right chain, never merges (ADR 0017). Agent PRs (authored by design4pro-agent, the cockpit's gh identity) and dependabot are excluded by author; pipeline labels exclude the race with om-open-pr. The standing develop-to-main promotion PR is opened with a maintainer's token - which is what makes `pull_request` workflows run on it at all, claude-code-review.yml among them - so the author filter cannot tell it apart from a hand-opened one, and no filter here reads the base branch. .github/workflows/promote-develop.yml therefore opens it carrying `merge-queue`, which `excludeLabels` already stands down on.

name: pr-review-threads
description: The `claude-review` job left unresolved review threads on a PR and applied `review-threads`; om-auto-fix-pr drives the PR to merge-ready and resolves them (ADR 0017). Without this the PR waits for a human to run the same skill by hand. `includePullRequests` is read by the design4pro/cezar fork the cockpit runs - stock cezar 0.11.0 drops every label event on a PR, so this automation does not fire without it. The gate is the label: only a collaborator or the Actions bot can set one, and the review job applies it once per head SHA. The run removes it as its first mutation, so a label still present is a run nobody took. The automation is only ever armed for pull requests targeting the integration branch: review-threads-label.mjs reads `baseBranch` from .ai/agentic.config.json and stands down on anything else, so the standing promotion - whose *head* is the integration branch, and which this run would therefore push follow-up commits straight onto - never arms one.

name: Triage new issues
description: A human adds `needs-triage`; afk-triage verifies the report, writes an Agent Brief comment and sets exactly one intake label. The label is the gate - only a collaborator can set one - which is also why this does not fire on `issue.opened` the way it does in cezar: om-auto-manage-issues already owns that event here, and two autonomous runs grooming the same fresh issue would race on its labels. Groom first, then ask for a brief.

name: Implement ready-for-agent issues
description: An issue labeled `ready-for-agent` is implemented test-first in a worktree from its Agent Brief, gated, opened as a PR and reviewed. Never merges. Distinct from `issue-autofix`, which answers the `autofix` label and drives an ungroomed issue end to end - these two never contend for the same issue because they watch different labels. `risk-high` and `security` are excluded: afk-triage never promotes those to `ready-for-agent` in the first place, and this is the second lock on the same door.

name: Spec to tickets
description: Weekday mornings: afk-to-tickets promotes the ticket frontier, then slices at most one newly merged spec into vertical tickets. Schedule rather than an event, so it never races the issue pipeline above: it reads `.ai/specs/` and the open tree, and only the frontier gets `ready-for-agent`. Idempotent - a spec that already has a parent issue is skipped.

task.prompt: Run the afk-to-tickets skill for {{project}} on {{date}}: promote the frontier, then slice at most one unsliced spec.

name: Weekly architecture review
description: Mondays: afk-architecture-review reads the last 30 days of hot spots and files at most three refactor issues, each with a recommendation strength. Read-only on code - the only writes are issues, and it never applies `ready-for-agent` itself: `Strong` gets `needs-triage` so triage writes the brief, `Worth exploring` gets `ready-for-human`. It reads `.ai/skills/afk-codebase-design/SKILL.md` for its vocabulary, so that repo-owned skill must exist here or the run has no shared terms to reason in.

task.prompt: Run the afk-architecture-review skill for {{project}} on {{date}}.

name: Weekly lessons
description: Fridays: afk-lessons turns mistakes repeated across the last 14 days of pull requests into enforced rules - mechanical ones into a lint rule, judgement into CODE_REVIEW.md, operational into AGENTS.md. A lesson seen only once is not a rule, so a quiet fortnight is a no-op, and it opens at most one pull request per run.

task.prompt: Run the afk-lessons skill for {{project}} on {{date}}.
